newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot resids steady to lower on mild weather.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot resids steady to lower on mild weather.

text.p: U.S. spot fuel oil prices were unchanged to slightly lower Wednesday in thin trade, with mild East Coast weather still undermining the complex, particularly low sulphur grades, industry sources said.
"I don't think summer is done in July, but we're adjusting down a little because of the weather and cheap gas prices," said one cash trader, noting low sulphurs seemed a bit toppy.
While East Coast temperatures are expected to warm slightly by the weekend, they are still not expected to rise much above normal right through the month.

New York Harbor 0.3 percent high pour slipped more than a quarter today to about $17.75 a barrel on reports of a 100,000 barrel HP deal for 8/5-10 delivery in the $17.70-17.80 range. Traders said expected late-month supplies, mild weather and competitive gas prices continued to pressure the grade.
Physical one percent in New York was unchanged to down slightly at about $17, traders said.
High sulphurs in New York held steady, with 2.2 percent still talked at $15.25-50.
At the U.S. Gulf, one percent fell 25 cents to just below the $16 mark, while three percent was stable at $14.50-75.
Traders said another high sulphur deal late Tuesday, this one at $14.62 (FOB Mississippi River) for 45,000 barrels loading next week, helped support the HSFO market.
USG August three percent paper was done at $13.90, with buyers and sellers still staddling $14. September was quoted at $13.75-90, while Q4 was pegged at $13.60-70.

New York city gate swing gas prices edged up a couple of cents Wednesday to $2.40/mmBtu, or $15.12 a barrel equivalent. Gas at Henry Hub, the NYMEX delivery point, firmed three cents to $2.20/mmBtu, or $13.86 a barrel.
